terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, so a canopy grid lands two by two on the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles. Nothing on it opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches to it -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides: no walls, no infill, no hanging goods. Market rows, food courts, bus stops and yard shelters across rural and peri-urban Thailand; a row of bays butted post to post is what a covered market is. Silver-brown sawn hardwood gone grey, palm thatch bleaching from tan to straw and blackening in the course shadows.

reasoning: ONE timber merge -- four posts, four head plates, eight knee braces, two king posts, the ridge beam, the ridge plank, six rafters and eight cord lashings; ONE thatch height grid carrying both slopes and the ragged eave; ONE InstancedMesh of eight purlins: THREE draw calls of 4.
Two materials of three: sawn timber (vertex colours -- post, plate, rafter, ridge plank, cord) and thatch. Both textureless, each with one post-construction canvas.
Repetition system: the purlin is the one part repeated at a fixed station, eight of them at four heights on each slope.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: At distance the identity is a low thatched gable on four posts with a ragged eave; close up it is the course structure of the thatch and the tied post-and-plate frame under it. The registry notes forbid modelled fronds, so the courses are a canvas and the eave silhouette is real geometry -- a per-column drop in the height grid's last rows, which is the one place a flat roof reads as thatch.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The roof stops ON the module edge rather than overhanging it. The plate and the proxy both show a freestanding shelter with a deep eave overhang; a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour, and the notes make the grid the contract.

The eave is the thatch TOP surface at 2.40 m, which is the reading that maximises pitch within the declared 3.20 m ridge. Reading it as the eave UNDERSIDE would put the top at 2.58 and drop the roof to 13.5 degrees.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 3.20 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the ridge along X. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment, and the two bays' corner posts then pair at the shared edge.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 150 mm posts at the corners carrying a head frame at 2.06-2.22 m with eight knee braces, a low gable above it with its ridge along X, thatch 180 mm thick from a 2.40 m eave to a 3.13 m apex, a sawn ridge plank capping it at 3.20 m, and a ragged eave hanging up to 110 mm below the eave line. Open on all four sides.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span exactly -2.000..+2.000 and nothing crosses it: the thatch stops on the module edge, the posts sit inside it with their outer faces on 2.000 less the 12 mm the cord lashings stand proud, and the ROTATED rafter boxes were shortened 50 mm because a box turned about X has an AABB half-depth of L/2 cos(s) + h/2 sin(s), which at the first build put the rafter ends at 2.016. The ROOF owns +-2.000 and every structural member stops short of it -- posts inset 12 mm, head plates 10 mm and shortened 20 mm, ridge beam and ridge plank shortened 20 mm -- because a frame whose bounding box shares a face with the roof's is four same-facing coplanar pairs of 4.07 m2 to check-coplanar, which cannot see that the surfaces never overlap in y. Clean at 0.001 m. y 0.000 to 3.200 at the top of the ridge plank. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 1.146 : 1.216, a SQUARE post grid of 0.769 x 0.765 H under a roof of 0.810 x 1.011 H, ridge along the narrow axis. Two divergences, both resolved for the notes and both recorded: the proxy OVERHANGS its post grid by 0.121 H at the eaves, which cannot be built because anything past 2.00 m collides with the next bay on a 4 m grid; and the proxy sits its eave at 0.61 of its height where the notes fix 2.40/3.20 = 0.75 for walk-under clearance. Honouring the notes caps the pitch at 20.0 degrees against the proxy's 39, which is why the ridge plank is 70 mm thick -- every millimetre off it is pitch. Post section IS taken from the proxy: 4 of 100 occupancy columns = 0.052 H = 0.166 m, built 0.150.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 1.146 : 1.216, post grid 0.769 x 0.765 H, roof 0.810 x 1.011 H, eave at 0.61 H, pitch 39 degrees. Used for the POST SECTION (0.052 H = 0.166 m) and for confirming that the post grid is square and the ridge runs across the narrow axis. NOT used for the overhang or the eave height: the registry notes fix a 4 m grid module whose roof may not cross the cell edge and whose eave is set by walk-under clearance, and that contract is the asset. The arithmetic of both divergences is in envelopeDerivation.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides, so the far side is the near side; the plate shows one gable end and one eave, which between them cover every distinct elevation.

componentTree.name: Timber post-and-plate frame, rafters and ridge
componentTree.topologyRationale: Four posts, four plates, eight braces, two king posts, a ridge beam, a ridge plank, six rafters and eight cord collars are one merge and one draw call, and the root the purlin instances hang off.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Posts 150 mm square at x,z +-1.913, y 0-2.06; head plates 120 x 160 mm on all four sides at y 2.06-2.22, outer faces on 2.000; knee braces 90 mm square at 45 degrees, 620 mm long, into both plates at every post; king posts 120 mm at x +-1.913 from 2.22 to 2.81; ridge beam 140 mm square at z 0 with its top on 2.95; ridge plank 4.00 x 0.07 x 0.34 m from 3.13 to 3.20; rafters 80 x 100 mm at x -1.913, 0 and +1.913, 2.056 m along a 20.0 degree slope; cord collars 170 mm square, 70 and 50 mm deep, at 2.00 and 1.88 m on every post.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The braces enter the post and plate as solids and stand inside the post section; the rafters are sunk 110 mm below the thatch underside so the purlins fit between them and nothing shares a plane with the roof; the ridge plank sits ON the thatch apex, overlapping it rather than meeting it. check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 0.60 m.

componentTree.name: Nipa palm thatch roof
componentTree.topologyRationale: One draped height grid carries BOTH slopes, so the gable is a row of the grid rather than two components -- one draw call for the whole roof, and the ridge crease comes out smooth-shaded, which is what a thatched ridge looks like.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A 20 x 12 height grid over x,z -2.00..2.00, 180 mm thick, top surface 3.13 m at z 0 falling to 2.40 m at |z| 2.00 with a 25 mm mid-slope sag; the last rows drop a per-column 0-110 mm, faded in over the outer third, so only the eave course is ragged.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The roof is the only thing at its heights; the ridge plank overlaps its apex and the rafters are sunk below its underside. Its edges are the grid's own wound strips, so no separate fascia shares a plane with it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with world UVs at 1.60 m.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: One pale straw albedo on a white material with a thatch multiply canvas; the course structure is entirely in the canvas, as the registry notes require.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: the two cord collars at each post head
localOverrides.evidence: crops/lashing.png #5c5851 sd 50 -- dark fibre cord wrapped twice at every post-to-plate joint; authored lifted to #8d7659 so the collar renders at ~95 against the gate's 58.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-timber (0.88) at #7a746d sd 28 (shaded post) and region-beam at #9f9890 sd 19 (sunlit head plate), with the ridge plank at #9b9997 -- a near-neutral silver-brown, R minus B only 13 to 21.

AUTHORED AS THE INVERSE OF THE HARNESS TRANSFER, not copied. Probed on two renders of the same post pixel: authored luma 147.5 rendered 66 at azimuth 0 and 49 at 180; authored luma 220.5 rendered 180 and 158. The harness key barely reaches a vertical face, so the plate's own value came back BELOW the backdrop's 58 -- the silhouette gate reading a leg as background. Solving for the plate's mean 130 gives authored luma 190, carried here as #d0cabe with post #c4beb2, plate #dad4c6, ridge plank #e8e2d4, rafter #b9b3a6 and cord #8d7659 as vertex colours on it. Measured back at 134 / 111 / 111 / 94 across the four azimuths, the darkest 1.6x the backdrop.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px sawn-timber multiply canvas after construction (fine longitudinal grain, four knots, three drying splits, cloudy silver weathering, three mould clusters), world UVs at 0.60 m. Deliberately weakly directional, because world UVs put v along a post but ACROSS a beam and a striped tile would read as a plank joint running the wrong way on half the frame.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-thatch (0.90) at #6d6257 sd 52 over the slope and region-thatchbutt (0.86) at #877e74 sd 40 along the exposed butts; the standard deviation of 52 IS the course structure, not noise.
Authored #9a8f78 and MEASURED BACK at 145-148 on the up-facing slope against the plate's own sunlit 143 -- right first time and left alone, unlike the timber.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px thatch multiply canvas after construction, world UVs at 1.60 m -- five courses per tile (0.32 m per course), 170 broad blade strokes 3-7 px wide, a butt line jittered per column, a pale lit-tip line above each butt and a shadow gradient below it, six thinned gaps. The tip-and-shadow PAIR is what makes the roof read as stacked layers; the first build had the shadow alone and read as wood grain.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components plus one repetition system: 3 of 4.

materials.note: timber and thatch: 2 of 3. Post, plate, brace, rafter, ridge plank and cord are vertex colours on one material, not six.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,592 of 4,000: 408 in the frame merge (34 boxes), 1,088 in the thatch height grid (two 20 x 12 smooth grids plus four wound edge strips), 96 in eight purlin instances.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes throughout the frame, several rotated onto the 45 degree braces and the 20.0 degree rafter slope; the roof is a height grid with thickness.
One InstancedMesh of eight purlins. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid; the module does not repeat itself.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction, ~2 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The proxy overhangs its post grid by 0.121 H at the eaves and sits its eave at 0.61 H against the notes' 0.75, so the built pitch is 20.0 degrees against the proxy's 39 and the built roof has no overhang at all.
risks.mitigation: The registry notes make the 4 m grid and the walk-under eave the contract, and a bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour. Both divergences and their arithmetic are recorded in envelopeDerivation and meshyNote; the proxy IS used for the post section and for confirming a square post grid and a ridge across the narrow axis.

risks.description: At 20.0 degrees and a 20 degree camera elevation the far slope is edge-on in the hero and the bay can read as a mono-pitch.
risks.mitigation: The gable is unambiguous at azimuth 90 and 270, which is where the turntable gate looks; the pitch is the highest the declared 2.40 eave and 3.20 ridge allow and the ridge plank was thinned to 70 mm to win the last of it.

risks.description: The bay is open on all four sides, so most of what the silhouette encloses is background: the volume under the roof, both gable voids, and the bays between the knee braces.
risks.mitigation: The turntable gate is run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement, and holeviz was read per azimuth to confirm the red covers the open volume and never a solid surface. Every timber face was lifted off the backdrop band first (darkest 94 against 58) so no solid part of the prop can be classified as a hole.
